upstream.note: The source the fork is compared against. If this pin changes, the whole inventory has to be measured again.

comparison: Built serially, with the same compiler and the same optimisation level (-O3) on both sides: the gate reads the compiler from the CMake cache of the fork build, builds upstream with it in .upstream/build_O3_gfortran<version>, and refuses to compare binaries whose .comment section names a different or mixed compiler version. Both the optimisation level and the compiler version change the outcome of some of the decks. Fields must be exactly equal; white space in header lines does not count. Differences that only show under OpenMP or MPI are therefore not seen by this gate -- those are covered by the stored ctest references.
memory_layout: Both binaries run under setarch -R, with a fixed memory layout. Without that pin, upstream 41.51 gave two answers from run to run on quad_dia2, quad_mdia and src_nobreak: in decks without breaking, FRABRE reads an unset KTETA (valgrind, BF-16). The fork sets that value and does not depend on the memory layout; the pin stays to keep upstream reproducible. Run with --no-pin to see the instability of upstream for yourself.

decks.note: Two fixes act on this deck; the field bugfix names the later one, and the fingerprints are those of both together. BF-16: the deck has no depth-induced breaking. In FRABRE, upstream divides by an unset KTETA, which gave Qb = 1 and switched the limiter off everywhere; the fork sets KTETA = 1 and computes with the limiter. On quad_dia2 without under-relaxation: upstream 100 iterations at 83%, the fork 28 iterations and converged. BF-62 (since 8 November 2026): the fork's semi-implicit DIA uses the consistent linearisation (QUADRUPLET 1 ... UPSTREAM for the upstream form).

decks.note: Attributed by measurement: with the repair reverted, this deck is bit-identical to upstream; with it, the deck differs. Upstream sets the breaking index to zero as soon as the biphase is not negative, after which HM = 0 drives SSURF into its saturated branch and destroys the wave field.

Deck without depth-induced breaking. In FRABRE, upstream divides by an unset KTETA, which gave Qb = 1 and switched the limiter off everywhere; the fork sets KTETA = 1 and computes with the limiter. On quad_dia2 without under-relaxation: upstream 100 iterations at 83%, the fork 28 iterations and converged.

Attributed by measurement (the same compiler and -O3 on both sides): with only the first stencil neighbour in the front ordering, as upstream does, the fork is byte-identical to upstream; with both neighbours it is byte-identical to upstream built with FFRO. Even serially, the front ordering decides the order in which the sweep updates the nodes, and at two boundary nodes upstream read a neighbour's value from the previous sweep. Up to 11% in the block file; the table at the centre point is equal.

The deck that lets this gate see the FFT path: on the flat bottom of qcm.swn the QC scattering is zero. The fork transforms with FFTW, upstream with FFTPACK; their rounding differs only in the last bits of double precision, which the single-precision fields almost never show. Measured: a change of 1e-9 in part of the transform output changes 350 of the 3234 output values, one of 1e-12 none. A larger deck (40 x 20 meshes, 36 directions, 30 frequencies) did show it once: Tm01 one unit in the last place at 1 of 861 points. Should this deck ever differ by such a single last-place value, the cause is that rounding, not a defect.
